subject: Physics
stem: An ideal gas undergoes four different processes from the same initial state as shown in the figure below. Those processes are adiabatic, isothermal, isobaric and isochoric. The curve which represents the adiabatic process among 1, 2, 3 and 4 is
solution:
\(\left(\dfrac{dP}{dV}\right)_{adiabatic} = -\gamma P\)

\(\left(\dfrac{dP}{dV}\right)_{isothermal} = -P\)

\(\left(\dfrac{dP}{dV}\right)_{adiabatic} > \left(\dfrac{dP}{dV}\right)_{isothermal}\)

The adiabatic curve is steeper than the isothermal curve, so the order (top to bottom) is Isobaric, Isothermal, Adiabatic, with Isochoric being the vertical line. Hence curve 2 is adiabatic.

stem: The angular speed of a fly wheel moving with uniform angular acceleration changes from 1200 rpm to 3120 rpm in 16 seconds. The angular acceleration in rad/s\(^2\) is
solution:
Angular acceleration \(\alpha = \dfrac{\omega_f - \omega_i}{t}\)

\(\omega_f = 3120 \times \dfrac{2\pi}{60}\) rad/s

\(\omega_i = 1200 \times \dfrac{2\pi}{60}\) rad/s

\(\Rightarrow \alpha = \dfrac{(3120 - 1200)}{16} \times \dfrac{2\pi}{60} = 4\pi\)

stem: In the given circuits (a), (b) and (c), the potential drop across the two p-n junctions are equal in
solution:
Potential drops across the p-n junctions will be same if either both junctions are forward biased or both junctions are reverse biased.

In figure (a) and (c), both junctions are forward biased therefore both have same potential.

In figure (b) first junction is forward biased and second junction is reverse biased, so both junctions have different potential difference.

stem: A biconvex lens has radii of curvature, 20 cm each. If the refractive index of the material of the lens is 1.5, the power of the lens is
solution:
Power of lens is given by

\(P = \dfrac{1}{f(m)}\)

\(\dfrac{1}{f} = (\mu - 1)\left(\dfrac{1}{R_1} - \dfrac{1}{R_2}\right)\)

\(\dfrac{1}{f} = \left(\dfrac{3}{2} - 1\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{20} + \dfrac{1}{20}\right)\)

\(f = 20\) cm

\(P = \dfrac{1}{20 \times 10^{-2}} = 5\) D

stem: A shell of mass \(m\) is at rest initially. It explodes into three fragments having mass in the ratio 2 : 2 : 1. If the fragments having equal mass fly off along mutually perpendicular directions with speed \(v\), the speed of the third (lighter) fragment is
solution:
Momentum of the system would remain conserved.

Initial momentum = 0

Final momentum should also be zero.

Let masses be \(2m\), \(2m\), and \(m\)

Momentum along \(x\)-direction = \(2mv\hat{i}\)

Momentum along \(y\)-direction = \(2mv\hat{j}\)

Net momentum \(= \sqrt{(2mv)^2 + (2mv)^2} = \sqrt{2} \cdot 2mv\)

Now, \(2\sqrt{2}mv = mv'\)

\(v' = 2\sqrt{2}v\)

stem: A long solenoid of radius 1 mm has 100 turns per mm. If 1 A current flows in the solenoid, the magnetic field strength at the centre of the solenoid is
solution:
We know, magnetic field at centre of solenoid

\(B = \mu_0 \dfrac{N}{\ell}I = \mu_0 n I\) where \(n = \dfrac{N}{\ell}\)

\(= 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \times 100 \times 10^3 \times 1\) where \(n = \dfrac{100}{10^{-3}}\)

\(= 4\pi \times 10^{-2}\) T

stem:
In the given nuclear reaction, the element \(X\) is

\(^{22}_{11}\text{Na} \rightarrow X + e^+ + \nu\)
solution:
The nuclear reaction is given as

\(^{22}_{11}\text{Na} \rightarrow {}^A_Z X + {}_{+1}e^0 + \nu\)

From conservation of atomic number

\(11 = Z + 1 \Rightarrow Z = 10 \Rightarrow \text{Ne}\)

From conservation of mass number

\(22 = A + 0 \Rightarrow A = 22\)

\(\therefore {}^A_Z X = {}^{22}_{10}\text{Ne}\)

subject: Physics
stem:
Given below are two statements

Statement I : Biot-Savart's law gives us the expression for the magnetic field strength of an infinitesimal current element (Idl) of a current carrying conductor only.

Statement II : Biot-Savart's law is analogous to Coulomb's inverse square law of charge \(q\), with the former being related to the field produced by a scalar source, Idl while the latter being produced by a vector source, \(q\).

In light of above statements choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct and Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect and Statement II is correct
solution:
According to Biot-Savart's law \(d\vec{B} = \dfrac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\dfrac{Id\vec{l} \times \vec{r}}{r^3}\) which is applicable for infinitesimal element. It is analogous to Coulomb's law, where \(Id\vec{l}\) is vector source and electric field is produced by scalar source \(q\).

Here statement I is correct and statement II is incorrect.

stem: The ratio of the radius of gyration of a thin uniform disc about an axis passing through its centre and normal to its plane to the radius of gyration of the disc about its diameter is
solution:
For axis through centre normal to plane:

\(I_1 = \dfrac{MR^2}{2}\)

\(k_1 = \sqrt{\dfrac{I_1}{M}} = \dfrac{R}{\sqrt{2}}\)

For axis about diameter:

\(I_2 = \dfrac{MR^2}{4}\)

\(k_2 = \sqrt{\dfrac{I_2}{M}} = \dfrac{R}{2}\)

\(\dfrac{k_1}{k_2} = \dfrac{R/\sqrt{2}}{R/2} = \sqrt{2} : 1\)

subtopic: Young's Double Slit Experiment - Fringe Width
stem: In a Young's double slit experiment, a student observes 8 fringes in a certain segment of screen when a monochromatic light of 600 nm wavelength is used. If the wavelength of light is changed to 400 nm, then the number of fringes he would observe in the same region of the screen is
solution:
\(\beta = \dfrac{\lambda D}{d}\)

Let length of segment of screen = \(l\)

\(\Rightarrow l = 8\beta_1 = \dfrac{8\lambda_1 D}{d}\) ...(1)

and \(l = n\beta_2 = \dfrac{n\lambda_2 D}{d}\) ...(2)

from (1) and (2)

\(8\lambda_1 = n\lambda_2\)

\(8(600 \text{ nm}) = n(400 \text{ nm})\)

\(n = 12\)

stem: A square loop of side 1 m and resistance 1 \(\Omega\) is placed in a magnetic field of 0.5 T. If the plane of loop is perpendicular to the direction of magnetic field, the magnetic flux through the loop is
solution:

\(\vec{B}\) and \(\vec{A}\) are in same direction, therefore

\(\phi_B = B.A = 0.5 \times 1^2 = 0.5\) Wb

stem: Two resistors of resistance, 100 \(\Omega\) and 200 \(\Omega\) are connected in parallel in an electrical circuit. The ratio of the thermal energy developed in 100 \(\Omega\) to that in 200 \(\Omega\) in a given time is
solution:
For parallel combination

\(P = \dfrac{V^2}{R}\)

\(\dfrac{P_1}{P_2} = \dfrac{R_2}{R_1}\)

\(\Rightarrow \dfrac{P_1}{P_2} = \dfrac{200}{100} = \dfrac{2}{1}\)

stem: The ratio of the distances travelled by a freely falling body in the 1\(^{st}\), 2\(^{nd}\), 3\(^{rd}\) and 4\(^{th}\) second
solution:
\(S_{n^{th}} = u + \dfrac{1}{2}a(2n - 1)\)

\(S_{1st} = \dfrac{1}{2}g(2 \times 1 - 1) = \dfrac{g}{2}\)

\(S_{2nd} = \dfrac{1}{2}g(2 \times 2 - 1) = 3\left(\dfrac{1}{2}g\right)\)

\(S_{3rd} = \dfrac{1}{2}g(2 \times 3 - 1) = 5 \times \left(\dfrac{1}{2}g\right)\)

\(S_{4th} = \dfrac{1}{2}g(2 \times 4 - 1) = 7 \times \left(\dfrac{1}{2}g\right)\)

\(S_{1st} : S_{2nd} : S_{3rd} : S_{4th} = 1 : 3 : 5 : 7\)

subtopic: Speed of Light in a Medium
stem: When light propagates through a material medium of relative permittivity \(\varepsilon_r\) and relative permeability \(\mu_r\), the velocity of light, \(v\) is given by (\(c\)-velocity of light in vacuum)
solution:
\(v = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\varepsilon_m \mu_m}}\)

\(v = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\varepsilon_0 \varepsilon_r \mu_0 \mu_r}}\)

Since \(c = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\varepsilon_0 \mu_0}}\)

\(\Rightarrow v = \dfrac{c}{\sqrt{\varepsilon_r \mu_r}}\)

stem: Two hollow conducting spheres of radii \(R_1\) and \(R_2\) (\(R_1 \gg R_2\)) have equal charges. The potential would be
options: Dependent on the material property of the sphere
solution:
Potential of conducting hollow sphere \(= \dfrac{KQ}{R}\)

Now, \(Q\) = same

\(\Rightarrow V \propto \dfrac{1}{R} \Rightarrow\) more the radius less will be the potential.

\(\Rightarrow\) Hence potential would be more on smaller sphere

subject: Physics
stem: A copper wire of length 10 m and radius \(\left(\dfrac{10^{-2}}{\sqrt{\pi}}\right)\) m has electrical resistance of 10 \(\Omega\). The current density in the wire for an electric field strength of 10 (V/m) is
solution:
Resistance, \(R = \rho\dfrac{L}{A} = \dfrac{L}{\sigma A}\)

\(\Rightarrow \sigma = \dfrac{L}{RA}\)

Also current density \(j = \sigma E = \dfrac{LE}{RA}\)

\(j = \dfrac{10 \times 10}{10 \times \pi\left(\dfrac{10^{-2}}{\sqrt{\pi}}\right)^2} = \dfrac{100}{10 \times \pi \times \left(\dfrac{10^{-4}}{\pi}\right)}\)

\(= 10^5\) A/m\(^2\)

solution:

\(\Rightarrow \text{Ratio} = \dfrac{\tan 30°}{\tan 45°} = \dfrac{1/\sqrt{3}}{1} = 1 : \sqrt{3}\)

stem: Plane angle and solid angle have
solution:
Plane angle \(= \dfrac{\text{Arc}}{\text{Radius}} = \dfrac{[L]}{[L]} \rightarrow\) Unit = Radian

\(= [M^0 L^0 T^0]\)

Solid angle \(= \dfrac{\text{Area}}{(\text{Radius})^2} \rightarrow\) Unit = Steradian

\(= \dfrac{L^2}{L^2} = [M^0 L^0 T^0]\)

\(\therefore\) Both have units but no dimensions

\(\Rightarrow \dfrac{T_1}{T_2} = \dfrac{E_0/4}{E_0/9} = \dfrac{9}{4}\)

solution:

stem: Two pendulums of length 121 cm and 100 cm start vibrating in phase. At some instant, the two are at their mean position in the same phase. The minimum number of vibrations of the shorter pendulum after which the two are again in phase at the mean position is:
solution:
\(T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{L}{g}}\)

Let \(n_1\) and \(n_2\) be integer.

\(n_1 T_1 = n_2 T_2\)

\(2\pi n_1 \sqrt{\dfrac{1.21}{g}} = 2\pi n_2 \sqrt{\dfrac{1.00}{g}}\)

\(\Rightarrow \dfrac{n_2}{n_1} = \dfrac{11}{10}\)

\(\therefore\) After completion of 11\(^{th}\) oscillation of shorter pendulum, it will be in phase with longer pendulum.

stem: A ball is projected with a velocity, 10 ms\(^{-1}\), at an angle of 60° with the vertical direction. Its speed at the highest point of its trajectory will be
solution:
At highest point vertical component of velocity become zero.

The angle with the vertical is 60°, so the angle with the horizontal is 30°.

At highest point speed of object = \(10\cos 30°\)

\(= 5\sqrt{3}\) m/s

stem: The truth table for the given logic circuit is (the circuit consists of NAND gates producing \(\overline{A \cdot B}\) and \(\overline{\overline{A} \cdot B}\), combined at a final AND gate to give output C)
solution:
\(C = \left(\overline{A \cdot B}\right) \cdot \left(\overline{\overline{A} \cdot B}\right)\)

\(\Rightarrow C = \overline{A \cdot B + \overline{A} \cdot B}\)

\(\Rightarrow C = \overline{(A + \overline{A})B}\)

\(\Rightarrow C = \overline{B}\)

The truth table would be

| A | B | C |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0 | 1 |
| 0 | 1 | 0 |
| 1 | 0 | 1 |
| 1 | 1 | 0 |

subject: Physics
stem: From Ampere's circuital law for a long straight wire of circular cross-section carrying a steady current, the variation of magnetic field in the inside and outside region of the wire is
options: Uniform and remains constant for both the regions.
A linearly increasing function of distance upto the boundary of the wire and then linearly decreasing for the outside region.
A linearly increasing function of distance \(r\) upto the boundary of the wire and then decreasing one with \(\dfrac{1}{r}\) dependence for the outside region.
A linearly decreasing function of distance upto the boundary of the wire and then a linearly increasing one for the outside region.
solution:
For solid wire

Inside point

\(B = \dfrac{\mu_0 I r^2}{R^2 \times 2\pi r} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I r}{R^2 \times 2\pi}\)

\(B \propto r\)

Outside point

\(B = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi r}\)

\(B \propto \dfrac{1}{r}\)

subject: Physics
stem: A series LCR circuit with inductance 10 H, capacitance 10 \(\mu\)F, resistance 50 \(\Omega\) is connected to an ac source of voltage, \(V = 200\sin(100t)\) volt. If the resonant frequency of the LCR circuit is \(\nu_0\) and the frequency of the ac source is \(\nu\), then
solution:
At resonance \(\omega L = \dfrac{1}{\omega C}\)

\(\omega = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{LC}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{10 \times 10 \times 10^{-6}}}\)

\(\omega = 100\)

\(\omega = 2\pi f \Rightarrow f = \dfrac{\omega}{2\pi}\)

\(\nu_0 = f_0 = \dfrac{100}{2\pi} = \dfrac{50}{\pi}\) Hz, since \(\omega = 100\)

\(\nu = f = \dfrac{100}{2\pi} = \dfrac{50}{\pi}\)

solution:

\(E \propto \dfrac{1}{R^3}\)

subtopic: Shear Modulus and Elasticity of Springs
stem:
Given below are two statements : One is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The stretching of a spring is determined by the shear modulus of the material of the spring.

Reason (R): A coil spring of copper has more tensile strength than a steel spring of same dimensions.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
solution:
It is true that stretching of spring is determined by shear modulus of the spring as when coil spring is stretched neither its length nor its volume changes, there is only change in its shape.

Tensile strength of steel is more than that of copper.

Hence Assertion is true and reason is false.

stem: A big circular coil of 1000 turns and average radius 10 m is rotating about its horizontal diameter at 2 rad s\(^{-1}\). If the vertical component of earth's magnetic field at that place is \(2 \times 10^{-5}\) T and electrical resistance of the coil is 12.56 \(\Omega\), then the maximum induced current in the coil will be
solution:
\(\phi_B = NBA\cos\omega t\)

\(\varepsilon = \dfrac{-d\phi_B}{dt} = -NBA\omega(-\sin\omega t)\)

\(\varepsilon = NBA\omega\sin\omega t\)

\(i_{max} = \dfrac{\varepsilon_{max}}{R} = \dfrac{NBA\omega}{R}\)

\(= \dfrac{1000 \times 2 \times 10^{-5} \times \pi(10)^2 \times 2}{12.56}\)

\(= 1\) A

subject: Physics
stem: The volume occupied by the molecules contained in 4.5 kg water at STP, if the intermolecular forces vanish away is
solution:
From ideal gas equation

\(PV = nRT\) where \(n = \dfrac{\text{mass of water}}{\text{mol. wt.}} = \dfrac{4.5 \times 10^3}{18}\)

\(V = \dfrac{nRT}{P}\)

At STP \(\Rightarrow T = 273\) K

\(P = 10^5\) N/m\(^2\)

\(V = \dfrac{4.5 \times 10^3}{18} \times \dfrac{8.3 \times 273}{10^5} = 5.66\) m\(^3\)

stem: Two transparent media \(A\) and \(B\) are separated by a plane boundary. The speed of light in those media are \(1.5 \times 10^8\) m/s and \(2.0 \times 10^8\) m/s, respectively. The critical angle for a ray of light for these two media is
solution:
\(\mu_A = \dfrac{3 \times 10^8}{1.5 \times 10^8} = 2\)

\(\mu_B = \dfrac{3 \times 10^8}{2 \times 10^8} = 1.5\)

For TIR, ray of light should travel from denser to rarer medium

\(\mu_A \sin\theta_C = \mu_B \sin 90°\)

\(2\sin\theta_C = 1.5\sin 90°\)

\(\sin\theta_C = 0.75\)

\(\theta_C = \sin^{-1}(0.75)\)
